lessons.title: 5 V's of Big Data
lessons.text: Volume = a LOT of data stored (size, years of records, many devices). Velocity = SPEED - data arriving fast / needs real-time reaction. Variety = DIFFERENT FORMATS mixed together (text + images + audio + tables). Veracity = TRUST/ACCURACY problem (duplicates, missing, inconsistent, dirty). Value = the data actually IMPROVED a decision or created benefit.

lessons.title: 4 Types of Analytics
lessons.text: Descriptive = What happened? -> dashboards, past totals, history only. Diagnostic = Why did it happen? -> investigating a cause, comparing logs/records after the fact. Predictive = What will happen? -> forecasts, estimates, churn/demand prediction. Prescriptive = What should we do? -> recommends an action, usually under constraints (budget, capacity). Tip: if it forecasts AND THEN recommends an action, it's Predictive -> Prescriptive in that order.

lessons.title: ETL
lessons.text: Extract (pull raw data from source) -> Transform (clean/standardize/convert) -> Load (store the finished data in the warehouse). Whatever verb the question uses tells you the stage: connects/retrieves/pulls = Extract; converts/standardizes/removes duplicates = Transform; stores in the warehouse = Load.

lessons.title: Data Types
lessons.text: Structured = fixed rows/columns/data types (like a spreadsheet). Semi-structured = has some organization (like JSON keys) but no fixed schema - different records can have different fields. Unstructured = free-form (text, images, audio) -> needs NLP (text) or computer vision (images) to analyze.

lessons.title: Internal vs External Sources
lessons.text: Internal = data the ORG ITSELF generated (its own POS, inventory, loyalty program). External = data from OUTSIDE the org (government stats, weather, market data) even if you use it internally.

lessons.title: Warehouse Traits (SITN)
lessons.text: Subject-oriented (organized around a business subject like customers/sales, not around one app). Integrated (combined/standardized from multiple systems). Time-variant (keeps historical data over time so you can compare periods). Non-volatile (data isn't overwritten - analysts mostly read, not update).

lessons.title: OLTP vs OLAP
lessons.text: OLTP = fast, current, transactional (recording a payment/order as it happens). OLAP = analyzing large historical volumes across many dimensions.

lessons.title: OLAP Operations
lessons.text: Slice = fix/restrict ONE dimension (e.g., just 2026). Dice = pick RANGES/subsets across SEVERAL dimensions at once (e.g., product + location + time together). Drill down = go from summary to MORE detail (year -> quarter -> month -> day). Roll up = go from detail to LESS detail (opposite of drill down).

lessons.title: Star vs Snowflake Schema
lessons.text: Star = ONE fact table with dimension tables connected DIRECTLY to it (simple, fast, fewer joins - preferred when you want simplicity/speed). Snowflake = dimension tables are further split into related sub-dimension tables (more normalized, but more joins -> more complex filter paths, harder to navigate).

lessons.title: Fact vs Dimension Tables
lessons.text: Fact table = the numbers/measures you're analyzing (sales amount, quantity, cost) plus foreign keys; grain = what one row represents (e.g., one row per product per order). Dimension table = descriptive attributes used to filter/group (product name, customer city, date). Relationship direction: ONE dimension row relates to MANY fact rows (one-to-many, dimension key = primary, fact key = foreign).

lessons.title: Common Power Query Fixes
lessons.text: Duplicate rows -> Remove Duplicates. Need columns from another table matched by a key -> Merge. Two tables, same columns, want to stack rows -> Append. Extra spaces / hidden characters in text -> Trim / Clean. Date read wrong (05/06 read as May 6 instead of June 5) -> Change Type Using Locale. Inconsistent spelling of the same category -> Replace Values or Conditional Column. Keep all rows from one table + only matching rows from another -> Left Outer Join.

cards.category: Quiz 3 - Data Cleaning and Transformation Transformation
cards.question: Same Order ID/product/amount appears twice after combining overlapping files
cards.answer: Select the identifying columns and choose Remove Duplicates
cards.explanation: you must pick which columns define “the same record” first.

cards.category: Quiz 3 - Data Cleaning and Transformation Transformation
cards.question: Why select unique-identifying columns BEFORE removing duplicates?
cards.answer: To ensure only records representing the same entity or transaction are removed
cards.explanation: otherwise you might delete records that only look similar but aren’t actually duplicates.

cards.category: Quiz 3 - Data Cleaning and Transformation Transformation
cards.question: One table says “Order Amount,” another says “Sales Value,” same meaning
cards.answer: before appending, Standardize the corresponding column names
cards.explanation: Append needs matching column names to stack correctly.

cards.category: Quiz 3 - Data Cleaning and Transformation Transformation
cards.question: Customer ID missing for several rows, and it’s essential for linking
cards.explanation: a critical missing value that can’t reasonably be guessed or filled in.

cards.category: Quiz 3 - Data Cleaning and Transformation Transformation
cards.question: Quantity shows -5, but quantities can’t be negative
cards.explanation: it violates a business rule (real-world impossibility), not just “missing.”

cards.category: Quiz 3 - Data Cleaning and Transformation Transformation
cards.question: “Metro Manila,” “NCR,” “National Capital Region” treated as 3 separate regions
cards.explanation: these are the same place, spelled differently.

cards.category: Quiz 3 - Data Cleaning and Transformation Transformation
cards.question: City field has ” Cebu City ” with extra spaces
cards.explanation: Trim removes leading/trailing spaces, Clean removes hidden non printable characters.

cards.category: Quiz 3 - Data Cleaning and Transformation Transformation
cards.question: Orders table (CustomerID, Amount) + Customers table (CustomerID, Name, City), want Name+City added to Orders
cards.answer: Merge using Customer ID as the matching field
cards.explanation: Merge pulls columns from another table via a shared key.

cards.category: Quiz 3 - Data Cleaning and Transformation Transformation
cards.question: Dates stored as TEXT sort alphabetically instead of chronologically
cards.answer: Convert the column to the Date data type
cards.explanation: text sorts by characters, not real date value.

cards.category: Quiz 3 - Data Cleaning and Transformation Transformation
cards.question: Two monthly tables, same column names/types, different row counts, want ONE combined table
cards.explanation: Append stacks rows on top of each other when structure matches.

cards.category: Quiz 3 - Data Cleaning and Transformation Transformation
cards.question: Gender recorded as “Female,” “F,” “Woman” - three spellings, one meaning
cards.answer: Replace Values or a Conditional Column
cards.explanation: both let you map variants to one standard value.

cards.category: Quiz 3 - Data Cleaning and Transformation Transformation
cards.question: 05/06/2026 should mean 5 June but is read as May 6
cards.explanation: this lets you specify the correct date format/region interpretation.

cards.category: Quiz 3 - Data Cleaning and Transformation Transformation
cards.question: Data is cleaned, but relationships still break and charts mislead
cards.answer: Analysis quality depends heavily on source-data quality
cards.explanation: the core lesson: garbage in, garbage out, even after some cleaning.

cards.category: Quiz 3 - Data Cleaning and Transformation Transformation
cards.question: Want ALL Orders rows plus matching customer info WHEN AVAILABLE, keeping unmatched orders too
cards.answer: Left outer join with Orders as the left table
cards.explanation: left outer join keeps every row of the “left”/main table regardless of a match.

cards.category: Quiz 3 - Data Cleaning and Transformation Transformation
cards.question: Student IDs like “00127” must keep leading zeros and won’t be used in math
cards.explanation: numeric types would drop the leading zero; Text preserves it exactly.

cards.category: Quiz 3 - Data Cleaning and Transformation Transformation
cards.question: Want to keep all rows but order them by region, then by amount high->low
cards.explanation: first sort key = region, second sort key = amount descending.

cards.category: Quiz 3 - Data Cleaning and Transformation Transformation
cards.question: Want only Central Visayas orders above 5,000 from September 2026
cards.explanation: three separate criteria (region + amount + date) applied together.

cards.question: Keeps 5 years of reservations to compare seasons/origins over time
cards.explanation: the warehouse preserves history across time periods for comparison.

cards.question: Analysts mostly READ; routine transactions don’t overwrite past values
cards.explanation: once loaded, warehouse data isn’t continually changed.

cards.question: Needs a repository ONLY for student services (enrollment/attendance/performance)
cards.explanation: a mart is a smaller, department/topic-specific repository (vs. a full enterprise warehouse).

cards.question: Needs to compare annual sales across regions/products with COMPLEX queries
cards.answer: A data warehouse optimized for analysis
cards.explanation: warehouses are built for this kind of heavy analytical querying, unlike operational databases.

cards.question: Moves from annual
cards.answer: quarterly -> monthly -> daily results -> Drill down
cards.explanation: going from summary to more detail.

cards.question: Sales amount, quantity sold, and profit being evaluated
cards.explanation: these are the numeric values you analyze/aggregate (as opposed to Dimensions, which describe/filter).

cards.question: Customer codes from different systems converted to ONE standard before storage
cards.explanation: combining and standardizing data from multiple sources is the “Integrated” warehouse trait.

cards.question: Wants to compare enrollment/performance/graduation/employment across several years
cards.explanation: combines multiple data types (integrated) over time (historical), exactly what a warehouse is built for.

cards.question: Dashboards/reports built from warehouse models sit in which architecture layer?
cards.explanation: the top layer users actually see and interact with.

cards.question: Must record thousands of payments QUICKLY and ACCURATELY, using current data
cards.explanation: fast, real-time transaction processing, not historical analysis.

cards.question: Views sales in Manila+Cebu during Q1, selecting ranges across product/location/time simultaneously
cards.explanation: multiple dimensions restricted at once = Dice (vs. Slice, which is only one dimension).

cards.question: Branch, product category, hour, day-of-week - what are these?
cards.explanation: descriptive fields used to break down/filter the data, not the numbers being measured.

cards.question: Order updates as it’s accepted
cards.answer: collected -> delivered (live, ongoing events) -> Operational database
cards.explanation: this is transactional/real-time activity, not warehouse analysis.

cards.question: Wants shared definitions and cross-department analysis (bookings/ops/maintenance/CS/finance)
cards.explanation: spans the WHOLE organization, unlike a single department data mart.

cards.question: Departments define “active customer” differently, causing conflicting reports
cards.answer: an EDW fixes this because It establishes common definitions and standards
cards.explanation: a shared, agreed-upon definition across departments.

cards.question: Combines historical transactions from Manila/Cebu/Davao for nationwide analysis
cards.explanation: designed exactly for combining and analyzing historical data across locations.

cards.question: Compares monthly payments across branches/customer groups using years of records
cards.explanation: multi-dimensional analysis over historical data.

cards.question: Organized around customers, products, sales, students (business topics, not one app’s structure)
cards.explanation: organized by business subject, not by source system.

cards.question: Enterprise warehouse feeds a smaller repository used only by finance
cards.explanation: a mart is a scoped-down subset of the full warehouse for one department.

cards.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
cards.question: A proposed dimension key has duplicate/blank values
cards.answer: must be fixed because A primary key must uniquely identify each row and should not be blank
cards.explanation: that’s the definition of a valid primary key.

cards.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
cards.question: Wants simple relationships, clear filter paths, efficient queries
cards.explanation: star schema is simpler and faster than snowflake because dimensions connect directly to the fact table.

cards.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
cards.question: Table has Product Key, Product Name, Category, Brand (descriptive fields, no numbers to sum)
cards.answer: It stores descriptive information for filtering and grouping
cards.explanation: this makes it a dimension table.

cards.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
cards.question: Connects sales with product/customer/branch/date so users can filter consistently
cards.explanation: building the structure of relationships between tables is data modeling itself.

cards.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
cards.question: Mixes monthly balances with individual transactions in the SAME fact table without distinguishing detail levels
cards.explanation: grain defines what one row represents; mixing two levels of detail breaks this.

cards.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
cards.question: Several bidirectional relationships create multiple filter routes (circular paths)
cards.answer: should Prefer single-direction filtering and avoid circular relationship paths
cards.explanation: bidirectional/circular filters cause ambiguous or incorrect results.

cards.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
cards.question: An order has 3 products, and the model records ONE ROW PER PRODUCT within that order
cards.answer: the grain is One row per product in each order
cards.explanation: literally describes what one fact-table row represents.

cards.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
cards.question: Which dimension tells you the selected products are smartphones?
cards.explanation: product category info lives in the product dimension table.

cards.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
cards.question: One product row relates to MANY sales rows
cards.answer: the cardinality from dimension to fact should be One-to-many
cards.explanation: one dimension entry, many matching fact entries.

cards.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
cards.question: Selecting a city in DimCustomer filters matching FactSales rows
cards.answer: this works because of A relationship through matching CustomerKey columns
cards.explanation: the relationship is what allows filters to flow from dimension to fact.

cards.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
cards.question: FactSales in the center, DimDate/Product/Customer/Branch connect directly to it
cards.explanation: fact table in the middle, dimensions directly attached, no sub-dimension layers.

cards.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
cards.question: ProductKey is TEXT in one table but a WHOLE NUMBER in the other
cards.answer: before relating them, Use compatible data types for both key columns
cards.explanation: relationships require matching data types on both sides.

cards.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
cards.question: Product, Category, and Department split into three related dimension tables
cards.explanation: dimensions normalized into further sub-tables.

cards.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
cards.question: Two tables with REPEATED keys connected directly produce unexpected totals
cards.explanation: repeated keys on both sides often signal an accidental many-to- many that inflates totals.

cards.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
cards.question: A report exposes technical key columns, keeps unused fields, and relies on implicit aggregation for KPIs
cards.answer: improve by Hide technical keys, remove unused fields, and create explicit DAX measures
cards.explanation: cleaner, safer, and more predictable than relying on default (implicit) aggregation.

cards.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
cards.question: Table has Sale ID, Date Key, Product Key, Quantity, Discount, Cost, Sales Amount
cards.explanation: it’s mostly numeric measures and foreign keys, the definition of a fact table.

cards.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
cards.question: “Total smartphone sales in Cebu during September” - where does the AMOUNT being summed come from?
cards.explanation: the fact table is always where you pull the numeric measure from; dimensions only filter/describe.

cards.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
cards.question: Users struggle because product filters must pass through category and department tables first
cards.answer: this is a Snowflake schema disadvantage: it creates more relationships and can complicate filter behavior
cards.explanation: more hops between tables = harder navigation.

cards.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
cards.question: DimProduct has one row for P101; FactSales has P101 in thousands of rows
cards.answer: DimProduct[ProductKey] is primary; FactSales[ProductKey] is foreign
cards.explanation: one-unique-row side = primary key, many-repeated side = foreign key.

questions.explanation: text sorts by characters, not real date value.

questions.category: Quiz 3 - Data Cleaning and Transformation Transformation
questions.question: Two monthly tables, same column names/types, different row counts, want ONE combined table
questions.explanation: Append stacks rows on top of each other when structure matches.

questions.category: Quiz 3 - Data Cleaning and Transformation Transformation
questions.question: Gender recorded as “Female,” “F,” “Woman” - three spellings, one meaning
options: Replace Values or a Conditional Column
questions.explanation: both let you map variants to one standard value.

questions.category: Quiz 3 - Data Cleaning and Transformation Transformation
questions.question: 05/06/2026 should mean 5 June but is read as May 6
questions.explanation: this lets you specify the correct date format/region interpretation.

questions.category: Quiz 3 - Data Cleaning and Transformation Transformation
questions.question: Data is cleaned, but relationships still break and charts mislead
options: Analysis quality depends heavily on source-data quality
questions.explanation: the core lesson: garbage in, garbage out, even after some cleaning.

questions.category: Quiz 3 - Data Cleaning and Transformation Transformation
questions.question: Want ALL Orders rows plus matching customer info WHEN AVAILABLE, keeping unmatched orders too
options: Left outer join with Orders as the left table
questions.explanation: left outer join keeps every row of the “left”/main table regardless of a match.

questions.category: Quiz 3 - Data Cleaning and Transformation Transformation
questions.question: Student IDs like “00127” must keep leading zeros and won’t be used in math
questions.explanation: numeric types would drop the leading zero; Text preserves it exactly.

questions.category: Quiz 3 - Data Cleaning and Transformation Transformation
questions.question: Want to keep all rows but order them by region, then by amount high->low
questions.explanation: first sort key = region, second sort key = amount descending.

questions.category: Quiz 3 - Data Cleaning and Transformation Transformation
questions.question: Want only Central Visayas orders above 5,000 from September 2026
questions.explanation: three separate criteria (region + amount + date) applied together.

questions.question: Keeps 5 years of reservations to compare seasons/origins over time
questions.explanation: the warehouse preserves history across time periods for comparison.

questions.question: Analysts mostly READ; routine transactions don’t overwrite past values
questions.explanation: once loaded, warehouse data isn’t continually changed.

questions.question: Needs a repository ONLY for student services (enrollment/attendance/performance)
questions.explanation: a mart is a smaller, department/topic-specific repository (vs. a full enterprise warehouse).

questions.question: Needs to compare annual sales across regions/products with COMPLEX queries
options: A data warehouse optimized for analysis
questions.explanation: warehouses are built for this kind of heavy analytical querying, unlike operational databases.

questions.question: Moves from annual
options: quarterly -> monthly -> daily results -> Drill down
questions.explanation: going from summary to more detail.

questions.question: Sales amount, quantity sold, and profit being evaluated
questions.explanation: these are the numeric values you analyze/aggregate (as opposed to Dimensions, which describe/filter).

questions.question: Customer codes from different systems converted to ONE standard before storage
questions.explanation: combining and standardizing data from multiple sources is the “Integrated” warehouse trait.

questions.question: Wants to compare enrollment/performance/graduation/employment across several years
questions.explanation: combines multiple data types (integrated) over time (historical), exactly what a warehouse is built for.

questions.question: Dashboards/reports built from warehouse models sit in which architecture layer?
questions.explanation: the top layer users actually see and interact with.

questions.question: Must record thousands of payments QUICKLY and ACCURATELY, using current data
questions.explanation: fast, real-time transaction processing, not historical analysis.

questions.question: Views sales in Manila+Cebu during Q1, selecting ranges across product/location/time simultaneously
questions.explanation: multiple dimensions restricted at once = Dice (vs. Slice, which is only one dimension).

questions.question: Branch, product category, hour, day-of-week - what are these?
questions.explanation: descriptive fields used to break down/filter the data, not the numbers being measured.

questions.question: Order updates as it’s accepted
options: collected -> delivered (live, ongoing events) -> Operational database
questions.explanation: this is transactional/real-time activity, not warehouse analysis.

questions.question: Wants shared definitions and cross-department analysis (bookings/ops/maintenance/CS/finance)
questions.explanation: spans the WHOLE organization, unlike a single department data mart.

questions.question: Departments define “active customer” differently, causing conflicting reports
options: an EDW fixes this because It establishes common definitions and standards
questions.explanation: a shared, agreed-upon definition across departments.

questions.question: Combines historical transactions from Manila/Cebu/Davao for nationwide analysis
questions.explanation: designed exactly for combining and analyzing historical data across locations.

questions.question: Compares monthly payments across branches/customer groups using years of records
questions.explanation: multi-dimensional analysis over historical data.

questions.question: Organized around customers, products, sales, students (business topics, not one app’s structure)
questions.explanation: organized by business subject, not by source system.

questions.question: Enterprise warehouse feeds a smaller repository used only by finance
questions.explanation: a mart is a scoped-down subset of the full warehouse for one department.

questions.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
questions.question: A proposed dimension key has duplicate/blank values
options: must be fixed because A primary key must uniquely identify each row and should not be blank
questions.explanation: that’s the definition of a valid primary key.

questions.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
questions.question: Wants simple relationships, clear filter paths, efficient queries
questions.explanation: star schema is simpler and faster than snowflake because dimensions connect directly to the fact table.

questions.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
questions.question: Table has Product Key, Product Name, Category, Brand (descriptive fields, no numbers to sum)
options: It stores descriptive information for filtering and grouping
questions.explanation: this makes it a dimension table.

questions.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
questions.question: Connects sales with product/customer/branch/date so users can filter consistently
questions.explanation: building the structure of relationships between tables is data modeling itself.

questions.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
questions.question: Mixes monthly balances with individual transactions in the SAME fact table without distinguishing detail levels
questions.explanation: grain defines what one row represents; mixing two levels of detail breaks this.

questions.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
questions.question: Several bidirectional relationships create multiple filter routes (circular paths)
options: should Prefer single-direction filtering and avoid circular relationship paths
questions.explanation: bidirectional/circular filters cause ambiguous or incorrect results.

questions.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
questions.question: An order has 3 products, and the model records ONE ROW PER PRODUCT within that order
options: the grain is One row per product in each order
questions.explanation: literally describes what one fact-table row represents.

questions.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
questions.question: Which dimension tells you the selected products are smartphones?
questions.explanation: product category info lives in the product dimension table.

questions.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
questions.question: One product row relates to MANY sales rows
options: the cardinality from dimension to fact should be One-to-many
questions.explanation: one dimension entry, many matching fact entries.

questions.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
questions.question: Selecting a city in DimCustomer filters matching FactSales rows
options: this works because of A relationship through matching CustomerKey columns
questions.explanation: the relationship is what allows filters to flow from dimension to fact.

questions.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
questions.question: FactSales in the center, DimDate/Product/Customer/Branch connect directly to it
questions.explanation: fact table in the middle, dimensions directly attached, no sub-dimension layers.

questions.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
questions.question: ProductKey is TEXT in one table but a WHOLE NUMBER in the other
options: before relating them, Use compatible data types for both key columns
questions.explanation: relationships require matching data types on both sides.

questions.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
questions.question: Product, Category, and Department split into three related dimension tables
questions.explanation: dimensions normalized into further sub-tables.

questions.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
questions.question: Two tables with REPEATED keys connected directly produce unexpected totals
questions.explanation: repeated keys on both sides often signal an accidental many-to- many that inflates totals.

questions.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
questions.question: A report exposes technical key columns, keeps unused fields, and relies on implicit aggregation for KPIs
options: improve by Hide technical keys, remove unused fields, and create explicit DAX measures
questions.explanation: cleaner, safer, and more predictable than relying on default (implicit) aggregation.

questions.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
questions.question: Table has Sale ID, Date Key, Product Key, Quantity, Discount, Cost, Sales Amount
questions.explanation: it’s mostly numeric measures and foreign keys, the definition of a fact table.

questions.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
questions.question: “Total smartphone sales in Cebu during September” - where does the AMOUNT being summed come from?
questions.explanation: the fact table is always where you pull the numeric measure from; dimensions only filter/describe.

questions.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
questions.question: Users struggle because product filters must pass through category and department tables first
options: this is a Snowflake schema disadvantage: it creates more relationships and can complicate filter behavior
questions.explanation: more hops between tables = harder navigation.

questions.category: Quiz 5 - Data Modeling for Business Intelligence Intelligence
questions.question: DimProduct has one row for P101; FactSales has P101 in thousands of rows
options: DimProduct[ProductKey] is primary; FactSales[ProductKey] is foreign
questions.explanation: one-unique-row side = primary key, many-repeated side = foreign key.
